arxiv-2307-14716.creator: David Moya
arxiv-2307-14716.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David Moya. A surface in a three-dimensional metric Lie group G G is said invariant if it is invariant with respect to a one-dimensional subgroup Γ \Gamma of the isometry group of G G .

arxiv-2308-12713.title: The quantum optics of gravitational waves
arxiv-2308-12713.creator: Enrico Junior Schioppa
arxiv-2308-12713.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Enrico Junior Schioppa. By utilizing quantum optics techniques, we examine the characteristics of a quantum gravitational wave (GW) signature at interferometers. In particular, we study the problem by analyzing the equations of motion of a GW interacting with an idealized interferometer. Using this method, we reconstruct the classical GW signal from a representation of the quantum version of an almost classical monochromatic wave (a single-mode coherent state), then we discuss the experimental signatures of some specific, more general quantum states.

arxiv-2401-07366.title: Stabilization of molecular hydrogen-bonded chains by carbon nanotubes
arxiv-2401-07366.creator: Alexander V. Savin, Yuri S. Kivshar
arxiv-2401-07366.description: Abstract We study numerically nonlinear dynamics of several types of molecular systems composed of hydrogen-bonded chains placed inside carbon nanotubes with open edges. We demonstrate that carbon nanotubes provide a stabilization mechanism for quasi-one-dimensional molecular chains via the formation of their secondary structures.

arxiv-2401-12881.title: Computing Diameter + 1 in Truly Subquadratic Time for Unit-Disk Graphs A conference version has appeared in the 40th International Symposium on Computational Geometry (SoCG 2024).
arxiv-2401-12881.creator: Hsien-Chih Chang, Jie Gao, Hung Le
arxiv-2401-12881.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hsien-Chih Chang, Jie Gao, Hung Le. Finding the diameter of a graph in general cannot be done in truly subquadratic assuming the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH), even when the underlying graph is unweighted and sparse. When restricting to concrete classes of graphs and assuming SETH, planar graphs and minor-free graphs admit truly subquadratic algorithms, while geometric intersection graphs of unit balls, congruent equilateral triangles, and unit segments do not.

arxiv-2406-03585.title: A Comparison of Recent Algorithms for Symbolic Regression to Genetic Programming
arxiv-2406-03585.creator: Yousef A. Radwan, Gabriel Kronberger, Stephan Winkler
arxiv-2406-03585.description: Abstract Symbolic regression is a machine learning method with the goal to produce interpretable results. Unlike other machine learning methods such as, e.g. random forests or neural networks, which are opaque, symbolic regression aims to model and map data in a way that can be understood by scientists.

pmc-10605529.title: Diagnostic Reference Levels in Interventional Pediatric Cardiology: Two-Year Experience in a Tertiary Referral Hospital in Latin America
pmc-10605529.creator: Ana M Aristizabal, Jaiber A Gutiérrez, Emmanuel Ramirez, Valentina Mejía-Quiñones, Carlos Ubeda, Walter Fernando Mosquera, Walter Mosquera, Bibhuti B Das
pmc-10605529.description: The goal of the present study was to propose the first local diagnostic reference levels (DRLs) for interventional pediatric cardiology procedures in a large hospital in Colombia. The data collection period was from April 2020 to July 2022. The local DRLs were calculated as the 3rd quartile of patient-dose distributions for the kerma-area product (Pka) values.

pmc-11484107.title: How to leverage implementation research for equity in global health
pmc-11484107.creator: Olakunle Alonge
pmc-11484107.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Implementation research (IR) is important for addressing equity in global health. However, there is limited knowledge on how to operationalize IR for health equity, and pathways for improving health equity through IR in global health settings. This paper provides an overview of guidance and frameworks for thinking about health equity as part of IR while noting the gaps in how this guidance and frameworks apply to global health.

pmc-11760210.title: Encountering the clinical complexity of type II Peters anomaly management approaches: a case report
pmc-11760210.creator: Devi Sarah Intan Permatasari, Dicky Hermawan, Rozalina Loebis
pmc-11760210.description: Anterior segment dysgenesis exerts its influence on a diverse array of ocular structures, encompassing the cornea, iris, ciliary body, anterior chamber and lens. We present a 20-month-old boy with bilateral corneal opacity. The visual acuity (VA) was 6/480 in both eyes. Upon examination, we found bilateral central corneal opacity with keratolenticular adhesions, anterior lens dislocation and opacification, aniridia.

pmc-12504161.title: Deficient DNA mismatch repair and Nectin-4 expression in upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC)

pmc-12504161.description: PurposeTo investigate the prevalence of deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) status in upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) and its association with clinicopathological characteristics as well as Nectin-4 immunohistochemical expression.MethodsWe retrospectively identified histologically confirmed UTUC cases treated at Peking University Third Hospital between December 2016 and September 2023.

pmc-12589540.title: Transcription factor ZNF263 primes human embryonic stem cells for pluripotency dissolution and lineage commitment
pmc-12589540.creator: Qianqian Yin, Jing Huang, Hongduo Sun, Shuhan Zhou, Linjie Ruan, Yi Zeng, Yana Li, Zhaohui Gong, Peiyu Chen, Xinbo Yuan, Jiafang Wan, Qingzhong Wang, Yuangao Wang, Haipeng Li, Naihe Jing, Xin Liu, Zhen Shao
pmc-12589540.description: Conventional human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) are capable of self-renewal and simultaneously poised for differentiation. But the mechanisms underlying this primed pluripotent state, which endows them with elevated responsiveness to differentiation cues, remain largely underexplored. Especially, little is known about the pivotal transcription factors (TFs) that orchestrate hESCs towards primed pluripotency.

pmc-12755204.title: Using a Proactive Telecare System to Support Independence, Health, and Well-Being in Older Adults: Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12755204.creator: Lauren Fothergill, Yvonne Latham, Niall Hayes, Carol Holland
pmc-12755204.description: BackgroundProactive telecare offers services designed to reduce the occurrence of emergency situations by delivering proactive outbound calls and follow-ups and providing information and advice. By engaging regularly with users, proactive telecare may foster social connections with older adults and enable the detection of changes in needs.

pmc-12984077.title: Characterizing Family 1 Glycosyltransferases (GT1, UGT) by Reverse Glycosylation: Fast Determination of Acceptor Specificity, Donor Specificity, Hydrolysis, and Enzyme Stability
pmc-12984077.creator: Mads R. Langhorn, David Teze
pmc-12984077.description: Manufacturing glycoside conjugates through conventional chemistry is a labor-intensive process that involves multiple reaction steps, generates substantial toxic waste, and often results in low yields with poor control over regioselectivity. In contrast, glycosyltransferase family 1 enzymes offer an efficient alternative, enabling the transfer of glycosyl groups in a single step with excellent regioselective control and high yields.

pmc-13455345.title: Phenotypic, genomic, and functional characterization of Corynebacterium sp. nov. isolated by droplet-based cultivation from vaginal swabs of a preeclampsia patient
pmc-13455345.creator: Junjie Yuan, Jing Wang, Hui Wang, Zhenzhen He, Zhongju Chen, Yating Hu, Xuan Zhou, Shaozhen Yan, Lijie Wei, Mengzhou He, Yi Jiang, Rui Su, Huihui Yu, Shaoshuai Wang, Weidong Tan, Wencheng Ding, Ling Feng, Zerui Wang
pmc-13455345.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMembers of the genus Corynebacterium are widely distributed across human mucosal surfaces and are increasingly recognized as important components of the female reproductive tract microbiota. However, their diversity is underestimated due to limitations of conventional cultivation approaches.ResultsIn this study, a novel bacterial strain, designated TJG_1T, was isolated from vaginal swab samples of a pregnant woman with preeclampsia (PE) using droplet-based microfluidic single-cell cultivation. Strain TJG_1T was characterized as a Gram-positive, non-spore-forming, non-motile short rod.

pmc-13669762.title: The future of dentistry in England: A vision for 2050 – From access crisis to health creation: Prevention, integration and public value
pmc-13669762.creator: Sara Hurley
pmc-13669762.description: By 2050, dentistry could be transformed by regenerative science, artificial intelligence, remote monitoring and more integrated digital records. The central question is whether those advances translate into better oral health for all or widen existing inequalities in access and outcomes. Many of the enabling technologies are already emerging; the more important question is how they are organised, commissioned and distributed.

pmc-13677787.title: Ribo-seq rRNA reads reveal co-predicted signatures of ribosome heterogeneity and collisions
pmc-13677787.creator: Edwin S Kyei-Baffour, William J Faller, Ferhat Alkan
pmc-13677787.description: Ribosome heterogeneity is increasingly recognized as a key factor in various biological contexts, including development, cancer, and immune responses. To enable systematic exploration of this diversity, we previously developed a bioinformatics method that utilized rRNA reads from Ribo-seq data, detecting changes in ribosomal protein composition (dripARF) and ribosome collisions (dricARF) between conditions simply and efficiently.

uslaw-usc-t42-s16535.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 149 (National Energy Policy And Programs); Subchapter XVII (Protecting America’S Competitive Edge Through Energy). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In general The Secretary shall establish distributed, multidisciplinary institutes (referred to in this section as “Institutes”) centered at National Laboratories to apply fundamental science and engineering discoveries to technological innovations relating.
